result.architecture_summary: The architecture has a sound core—durable repository state, bounded workers, deterministic graph checks, isolated changes, runtime evidence, append-only recovery, and human design authority. The current implementation, however, is dominated by a one-time global reconciliation system whose correlated LLM verification, prompt accretion, and stale-canon handling are unsuitable for an evolving GDD. It has optimized confidence in a bootstrap graph before proving repeatable Unity feature delivery.
result.verdict_reason: Keep the core control boundaries, but replace global semantic convergence with a thin, canon-versioned vertical-slice loop. The present system cannot safely synchronize changing canon: its RAG is already stale, tasks lack requirement-version bindings, completed work cannot become stale, and readiness trusts declared status rather than merge/test evidence. It is also materially overbuilt relative to one completed gameplay feature and does not yet demonstrate days-instead-of-weeks leverage.
strong_decisions: Repository artifacts, not chat memory, own durable state.
Graph identity, dependency integrity, acyclicity, and basic readiness are deterministic rather than reconstructed by an LLM.
Reconciliation cannot directly mutate the operational graph, and initial seeding required explicit human approval.
Workers do not declare themselves complete; merge and external evidence are intended to control completion.
Static approval can be overturned by Unity/runtime evidence.
Repair attempts are bounded, no-op refinements consume budget, and history is preserved.
Parallel coding is deferred until single-ticket execution is reliable.
Design-gap detection is separated from permission to invent missing design.
structural_flaws: Root canon conflates game design, engineering architecture, AI workflow, token policy, repository observations, scene inventory, and file-lock rules. This creates circular authority and embeds facts that will become stale.
The verifier is not meaningfully independent: all auditors/refiners use the same Claude CLI and prompt family, inspect the same candidate framing, and largely alternate only between Opus and Sonnet.
Finding severity is model-assigned. Only blocker/error counts as material, so credible warnings can survive into an approved graph; duplicate NSC-003 criteria and other warnings did so.

Verifier and refiner prompts are heavily anchored to the bootstrap answer. The 1,979-line reconciliation prompt and 976-line refiner prompt contain dated, mechanic-specific closure rules that may conflict with later canon.
`taskcontrol ready` proves only structural eligibility. It does not verify GDD freshness, merge state, acceptance evidence, Unity results, or whether a completed dependency has regressed.
There is no implemented evidence-backed state transition, completion command, stale/superseded state, or reconciliation graph-diff/apply workflow.
The architecture assumes targeted RAG will ground workers, but the existing corpus is already contradictory to current canon and has no freshness gate.
Planning, implementation, evaluation, refinement, reconciliation, and human-facing status each produce overlapping declarations of truth without a single current evidence manifest.
observed_failure_solutions: Human Unity feedback re-entering GER solved two observed camera failures that static evaluators passed.
The Assets delta/no-op guard addresses an observed refiner that reported `implemented` without changing the project.
Append-only runtime feedback and immutable reconciliation runs address lost/overwritten diagnostic history.
Source-boundary filtering addresses observed use of forbidden or fabricated evidence.
Dangling-dependency repair, semantic graph validation, and deterministic identity checks address failures encountered during reconciliation.
Timeout/max-turn recovery and resumable verification address actual long-running-agent failures.
Human Play Mode testing found a door progress-fill rendering defect missed by static review; the resulting regression test protects that exact failure.
Separating current views from immutable run history addresses prior provenance/layout confusion.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Artifact Authority plus multi-evaluator artifact GER protects future AI-generated design, but no production artifact dependency exists yet.
Claims, leases, GitHub Projects mirroring, Draft PR orchestration, and merge queues address future multi-worker operations.
Exclusive-resource scheduling is sensible metadata but primarily protects concurrency that is explicitly deferred.
Fifteen parallel auditors, streaming field repairs, semantic conflict clusters, and arbitration mostly protect failures created by the global reconciliation strategy itself.
Continuous backlog replenishment, autonomous scheduling, simulation agents, and project-wide budget governance remain prospective.
Broad project scanning, incremental caches, Roslyn analysis, and full progressive decomposition have not yet been justified by a real blocked feature.
overengineering: The successful verification involved 28 auditor calls totaling 8,863.99 recorded model-seconds, plus eight repair proposals and conflict arbitration; token/cost usage was not retained.
The approved reconciliation run contains 112 files and occupies 5.7 MB. `Pipeline/Reconciliation` occupies 7.8 MB versus 156 KB for `Assets/NoSafeCircle`.
Reconciliation contains roughly 20.6k non-JSON/non-Unity/non-meta lines across 146 files, before the proposed supervisor, context platform, or production validation layer exists.
Repository history shows dozens of consecutive fixes for reconciliation closure, provenance, source boundaries, max turns, identity ordering, false positives, and recovery over four days.

From the initial GER baseline to the frozen commit, the repository gained about 131k inserted lines across 379 files, largely pipeline/output machinery, while the work graph still records only the camera as complete.
The full 9,216-word GDD is small enough that explicit section bindings are currently safer and cheaper than operating a generic RAG platform.
missing_components: Stable requirement IDs and a GDD revision/hash bound to every task, artifact, context pack, and evidence result.
A deterministic canon-freshness gate; the current retriever validates shape and chunk count but not correspondence with the current GDD.
Requirement-level GDD change detection that marks affected tasks/artifacts `stale`, `superseded`, or `needs_revalidation`.
An evidence-backed task transition command that verifies commit/merge identity and required validation artifacts before completion.
A Windows Unity execution adapter producing compilation logs, NUnit XML, scene-build results, screenshots, and runtime observations.
A blind semantic diff review whose reviewer receives the current requirement revision, diff, and test evidence without implementer reasoning or reconciliation conclusions.
Token, cost, retry, and human-time accounting; current Claude envelopes are reduced to structured output and duration.
A concise human decision queue and current-state projection derived from authoritative manifests rather than manually synchronized prose.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary boundaries are: human-approved game canon; engineering ADRs; versioned task intent; integrated repository state; validation evidence; transient worker state; and human acceptance of design/game-feel decisions.
The GDD should own player-facing design, not AI architecture, token ceilings, current scene inventory, or exact repository locks. Those belong in ADRs or generated project-state evidence.
`Tasks/*.yaml` can own planned intent, but cannot independently be authority for implementation completion. Completion needs a merge-bound evidence manifest.
Transient claims and retries belong in a run journal; mirroring them into both GitHub and task files would duplicate responsibility.
Reconciliation snapshots are useful audit records, but the mutable current view, approval manifest, bootstrap marker, task files, GER final result, and prose status already disagree in places.
`CURRENT_STATE.md` says Assignment 7 is unimplemented despite a committed working Assignment 7 pipeline and outputs.
`outputs/current/STATUS.md` says human bootstrap approval remains required despite the approval and persisted-bootstrap manifests.
The GER machine result says `accepted_static` with a tripped breaker, while prose reports later final manual acceptance. Downstream automation cannot safely infer the authoritative disposition.
gdd_iteration_concerns: The implemented system provides one-time bootstrap correctness, not synchronization with evolving canon.
The existing RAG corpus says WASD movement and hold-to-open interaction, while current canon requires mouse click/hold movement and click-to-approach automatic door timing.
Tasks contain prose citations but no stable requirement IDs or GDD version/hash. A changed paragraph cannot be mapped deterministically to affected work.
A completed task remains complete after canon changes; `taskcontrol ready` may therefore unlock dependents against obsolete behavior.
Open task contracts, tests, approved artifacts, and context caches also remain trusted until a human notices drift or performs another global reconciliation.
Approved design artifacts are declared subordinate to the GDD but have no implemented invalidation/supersession mechanism when their parent requirements change.

Full reconciliation after every material change will re-interpret the whole graph, creating key/edge/severity churn. The correct unit is requirement-level impact analysis followed by targeted re-planning.
Project-specific closure instructions in verifier prompts can anchor later models to yesterday's design even when the GDD changes.

When canon changes after implementation, the system should preserve the historical acceptance record, mark the affected implementation stale, create an explicit migration/revalidation item, block dependents where necessary, and require human approval only for the semantic decision—not reconstruct the entire roadmap.
result.throughput_assessment: Major near-term leverage is not yet demonstrated. The camera experiment proves that an agent/refiner can accelerate coding once a task is bounded, but it required repeated static passes and manual Unity feedback. The bootstrap consumed substantial infrastructure and semantic-audit effort without delivering another gameplay feature. With Unity unavailable inside the agent environment, scene rebuilding, compilation, visual inspection, game feel, and final acceptance remain human bottlenecks. A thin single-feature loop could plausibly save time; the full planned milestone chain is more likely to delay the game than produce it in days.
human_intervention_points: Approve GDD changes, missing design, generated design artifacts, and architecture-affecting decisions.
Playtest movement feel, camera framing, encounter pressure, readability, balance, and other experiential criteria that deterministic tests cannot establish.
Run or supervise Unity Editor operations until a trustworthy Windows Unity adapter exists.
Inspect scene, prefab, Input Actions, ProjectSettings, package, and generated-art integration.
Review bounded escalations after repeated failures, ambiguous canon, or scope expansion.
Approve merges and any task/artifact invalidation caused by changed canon.
Curate the near-term vertical-slice priority; autonomous scheduling cannot decide product value reliably from graph structure alone.

next_slice.title: Deliver NSC-003 through a thin canon-versioned Unity loop
next_slice.why: NSC-003 is visible gameplay, unlocks several consumers, directly exposes the stale-RAG problem, and exercises execution, Unity validation, recovery, and evidence-backed completion. No generic scanner, decomposer, or supervisor is needed to learn whether the pipeline can actually save time.
deliverables: Create a compact, checked context manifest containing the current GDD commit/hash, exact movement requirement excerpts, NSC-003 contract, relevant files, and current repository observations. Do not consume the stale Assignment 4 corpus.
Remove duplicated acceptance language and bind the task to stable requirement identifiers for this slice.

On one branch/worktree, implement mouse click-to-destination and hold-to-steer movement, shared pointer-plane projection, restriction/reset/suspend APIs, Input Actions changes, scene-builder wiring, and focused tests.
Run Windows Unity compilation, EditMode tests, PlayMode tests, scene regeneration, and a short human movement-feel/framing check. Persist XML/log/screenshot/manual evidence.
Perform one fresh semantic diff review using only the versioned contract, diff, and validation evidence.
Merge, then update NSC-003 through an evidence-bound transition that records merge commit, GDD hash, test artifacts, elapsed time, model calls, token/cost usage, retries, and human minutes.
next_slice.proof_of_value: NSC-003 is merged and playable in less than one working day; all Unity checks pass; no stale-canon input is used; task completion is tied to evidence; downstream readiness changes deterministically; and measured total effort is lower than an ordinary manual implementation.

do_not_build_yet: A generic RAG service or incremental vector/index infrastructure
Progressive Decomposer and Artifact Authority platform
Additional reconciliation auditors, prompt closure rules, streaming repair, or arbitration
GitHub Projects synchronization and dependency mirroring
Parallel coding workers and lease expiry
Automatic artifact generation before a real design gap blocks a near-term slice

alternative_architecture.description: Use a thin event-driven vertical-slice architecture. State: separate versioned game requirements, engineering ADRs, a small rolling work ledger, transient run journals, and immutable evidence manifests. Planning: human chooses the next player-visible slice; one bounded planner may split only that slice, with tasks bound to requirement IDs/revisions. Execution: one coding agent works in one branch/worktree from explicit canon excerpts and targeted `rg`/Unity evidence. Validation: run deterministic Git, compile, EditMode, PlayMode, scene-build, and artifact checks first; then one blind semantic diff review; require human playtesting only for experiential criteria. Recovery: checkpoint each phase, retain the branch/logs, permit at most one or two evidence-directed repairs, then escalate. Unity integration: a small Windows host adapter invokes Unity batch mode and returns XML/logs/screenshots; scene/prefab/Input Actions changes remain human-reviewed. GDD changes: compute a deterministic requirement diff, mark only referenced tasks/artifacts stale, run one bounded impact-analysis model, and apply human-approved migration tasks rather than globally reconciling the roadmap.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It preserves the valuable safety properties—durable state, restartability, bounded spending, independent evidence, human authority, and merge isolation—while removing correlated global semantic convergence. It makes moving-canon synchronization local and explicit, puts deterministic checks at freshness/completion boundaries, and measures success by merged playable slices rather than graph polish.

evidence.observation: The corpus identifies a July 30 source and still states WASD movement, hold-to-open doors, and asset-pack scope, contradicting current canon.
Its explicit policy says not to use Assignment 4 RAG and to rebuild it from the current GDD before reintroducing retrieval.
The 349-line document mixes gameplay, AI architecture, token budget, current repository observations, exact scene-builder locks, and human integration rules as root canon.
The task has no requirement IDs or GDD hash/version and contains two near-duplicate gameplay-suspend acceptance criteria that survived approval.
Readiness checks only declared status, kind, execution scope, and dependency statuses; it does not inspect merge, evidence, canon freshness, or repository behavior.
Bootstrap hashes are deliberately historical; live task status changes are accepted without evidence validation.
Auditors invoke the same Claude CLI; severity is model-selected, and material findings are mechanically limited to blocker/error.
The verification uses 15 scoped auditors, same-provider model aliases, streaming repairs, arbitration, and selective pass-two reuse.
The prompt is 1,979 lines and contains extensive project-specific dependency and mechanic instructions, increasing anchoring and future-change risk.
The 976-line prompt contains dated VERIFIED CLOSURE sections and hard-coded current movement, spell, enemy, restart, door, and resource-lock conclusions.

Pass one produced 56 findings/21 material findings; final verification still contained 30 findings but zero classified material findings. The run used 28 recorded auditor calls and eight repair proposals.
The current view says human approval is still required even though APPROVED_BOOTSTRAP.json and BOOTSTRAP_PERSISTED.json exist.
It says Assignment 7 is not implemented despite the committed Assignment7StyleGuide pipeline and successful output artifacts.
Two camera implementations passed static evaluation but failed in Unity; a later refiner made no Assets changes, requiring runtime feedback and no-op detection.
Machine state remains `accepted_static` with a tripped circuit breaker and notes that Unity is unavailable, while the README separately reports final manual acceptance.
The sealed-door implementation passed static validation before human Play Mode testing found a progress-fill rendering defect; all Unity compilation and scene checks were human responsibilities.
Tests still assert WASD and Hold E HUD text, demonstrating how previously valid implementation evidence becomes obsolete as the GDD evolves.
